candidates.title: BPR-0966: which surface owns Dif while a workshop edit is on Compose?
candidates.revision: 12ea8646 (src and tests identical to main faf53c8f); course exe 86de5254…85be, canary 109315a6…cc
criteria: BPR-0966 AC1: while a workshop proposal is shown and accepted on the Compose review page, which surface owns the single Dif widget, and do the ready and acknowledge cues stay required there?
options: A visible workshop slot on Compose: Dif moves there and plays ready and acknowledge
The bottom-left corner, decided together with BPR-0800: Dif rests there on Compose and plays the cues there
No Dif on Compose: amend RFC-BPR-0031 B7 so ready and acknowledge are not required on that page
Other: my answer is in the note
candidates.content:
What happens now. When an agent proposes a workshop edit, the app opens the dedicated Compose review page (RFC-BPR-0037) and then presents Dif. Opening Compose hides every drawer, including the conversations drawer that holds the AI tools slot. Dif lives only in that slot (RFC-BPR-0031 B6), so on Compose Dif is hidden and the two workshop cues never play. The draft itself is right: the exact proposed and accepted bytes, one acceptance, one sprite and zero GitHub publication all pass.

Observed on the exact candidate just now (application_agent_finding_dif_context_contract, 19.1 s, macOS arm64):
agent-finding-dif-workshop-visibility: proposal-editor=1 proposal-ai-slot=0 proposal-dif=0 accepted-editor=1 accepted-ai-slot=0 accepted-dif=0 painted-consider=1 painted-ready=0 painted-acknowledge=0

Why it needs you. RFC-BPR-0031 B7 lists acknowledging an accepted workshop edit as one of Dif's ten ordinary paths, so the course still expects ready after the proposal and acknowledge after acceptance. Deleting those two assertions would silently drop B7; moving Dif changes placement. BPR-0800 (Dif rests in the bottom-left corner on review surfaces) already reserves the corner-versus-slot decision for review surfaces, and your accepted Home corner does not decide Compose.

The choices. A visible workshop slot: Compose gains a small AI tools area and Dif plays both cues there. The corner: Dif sits at the status bar's leading edge on Compose (the Home size, no pointer or focus path) and plays the cues there; this also answers part of BPR-0800. No Dif on Compose: RFC-BPR-0031 B7 is amended so the two cues are not required on that page, and the course stops expecting them. Pick one. If you would rather settle it in a separate design session, choose Other and say so. Windows is deferred and not part of this question.
